clue.text: Plant donor leg set by doctor, initially

indicators.note: set here means arranged anew, so the letters of donor leg are put into a fresh order
initially asks for only the opening letter of the word doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor fits a donated leg beside a plant, perhaps in some odd surgical garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' scrambles DONOR LEG into GOLDENRO; 'initially' adds the D from doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a tall yellow-flowered perennial of the daisy family, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: A writer's turf

definitions.meaning: Günter ... was a German novelist, author of The Tin Drum
turf is ...-covered ground, the green sward itself

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is' joining the two definitions: a writer is turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass the novelist bears the surname, and turf is the lawn plant growing over soil.

clue.text: Shackle produced by Roman soldiers seizing rebel leader

indicators.note: seizing means the soldiers grab and hold the next letter inside themselves

parts.note: a legion was a large unit of the Roman army

indicators.note: leader points to the front letter of the word rebel

explanation.surface: Roman troops capture the head of a revolt and put him in chains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes R from rebel; 'seizing' puts it inside LEGION.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg iron is a metal fetter locked round a prisoner's ankle, a type of shackle.

clue.text: Peers around rough entrances crossed by golfer

indicators.note: crossed by means the golfer's name goes across and encloses the chosen letters

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African major-winning golfer

indicators.note: entrances points to the opening letters of the words around and rough

explanation.surface: Noblemen wander round the rough while a golfer strides across their path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrances' takes A and R from 'around rough'; 'crossed by' puts them within ELS. 'Peers' looks like a verb of looking, but it means nobles.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are titled nobles ranking in the British peerage, hence peers.

clue.text: Figure old motor starter is installed in right-hand vehicle

indicators.note: is installed in means these letters are fitted inside the vehicle pieces

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

indicators.note: starter picks the first letter of the word motor

explanation.surface: An old engine's starter motor is fitted into a right-hand-drive vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' gives the first letter of motor, and 'is installed in' sets it with O in the vehicle. 'Figure' means a geometric shape, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric shape with four equal sides, a plane figure.

clue.text: Doing, as is ordered, what's expected from a GP

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing things as instructed is just what a family doctor expects of patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges DOINGASIS. A GP is a general practitioner, the British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A family doctor is expected to identify a patient's illness; that identification is the medical verdict.

clue.text: Heard 'Clear off!' in a broad brogue, say

indicators.note: Heard tells us we want a word that sounds the same as the exclamation
in a broad accent suggests the word is spoken aloud rather than written

parts.note: shoo is the word shouted to send someone or something away

explanation.surface: Someone yells 'Clear off!' in a thick Irish brogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Brogue misleads as an accent, which fits 'Heard' and 'broad', but it is the sturdy leather footwear; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a stout leather lace-up with decorative perforations, an example of footwear.

clue.text: Sublime member of singing group

definitions.meaning: highest or most excellent, as sublime does
the ... were Motown's famous female vocal trio, so one of them is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means of the highest excellence, and Diana Ross's Motown trio were the Supremes.

clue.text: Musical works in which Hamlet's friend's first to go burying gold

indicators.note: burying means the remaining letters hold the next piece deep inside them
first to go means the opening letter of the friend's name is dropped

parts.note: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend in Shakespeare's play, with the possessive S kept
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Large choral works in which Hamlet's companion is the first to die, after burying treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to go' leaves ORATIOS, which 'burying' opens to take the heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorios are large-scale sacred compositions for choir, soloists and orchestra, a kind of music.

clue.text: Bounder showing angora creation — knockout all round

indicators.note: all round means the knockout letters wrap around the remaining piece

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout

indicators.note: creation means something newly made out of the word angora, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cad shows off a fluffy angora garment that is a total knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creation' gives ANGARO and 'all round' wraps the boxing abbreviation about it. 'Bounder' looks like an old word for a cad; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo moves by leaping, so it is literally an animal that bounds.

clue.text: Attraction of climber getting into lap dancing

indicators.note: getting into means the climber goes inside the rearranged letters
dancing means the letters of lap move about into a new order

parts.note: the pea plant climbs with tendrils, so it is a climber

explanation.surface: The draw of a mountaineer who has taken up lap dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' gives APL and 'getting into' opens it after its second letter. 'climber' wants to be a mountaineer; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is the quality of being attractive or interesting, so it means attraction.

clue.text: Accordingly, returned flag as an object of worship

indicators.note: returned means the word for accordingly is turned back to front

parts.note: so means therefore or accordingly
the flag or yellow flag is a wild iris

explanation.surface: A banner brought back is treated as something to be revered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SO into OS. 'flag' looks like a banner, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and the underworld, so he was worshipped.

clue.text: Long streamer displayed by group, role-playing

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians or people

indicators.note: playing means the letters of role are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A band at a role-playing game unfurls a long ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the letters in front of it. The compound 'role-playing' is split into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A banderol is a long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast or lance.

clue.text: Figures holding back in game

indicators.note: holding means the figures enclose the next piece

parts.note: tens are numbers, figures

indicators.note: back means the little word in is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Figures, presumably scores, hold someone back in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the little word round and 'holding' sets it before the last letter of the figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net, a game.

clue.text: Two litres covered by one-time liquid softener

indicators.note: covered by means the litres are wrapped inside the anagram that follows
liquid means fluid, not fixed, so the letters of one-time flow into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for litre, so two litres give LL

explanation.surface: A couple of litres of some old liquid fabric softener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' gives EMOIENT and 'covered by' splits it after its third letter for the litres.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a preparation that soothes and softens the skin, so it is a softener.

clue.text: Typical sort of characters, as in 'serfs', maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the quoted letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are an anagram

explanation.surface: Characters such as serfs are typical of a certain sort of story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges ASINSERFS. 'Typical' hides 'type': this is a sort of typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans serif is a typeface whose letters lack small finishing strokes, a kind of printed character.

clue.text: Out of control city mess affecting an entire body

indicators.note: out of control means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An unruly urban mess that infects the whole populace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of control' rearranges CITYMESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A systemic condition spreads through the whole organism rather than one part.

clue.text: Prone to an outburst against rough calico around neck opening

parts.note: V for versus is the standard abbreviation for against

indicators.note: around means the jumbled cloth letters surround the next piece
rough means roughly handled, so the letters of calico are jumbled
opening picks the first letter of the word neck

explanation.surface: Someone apt to explode over a scratchy calico garment's neckline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns CALICO into OLCAIC; 'opening' gives N, which 'around' puts inside it after V.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic temperament erupts suddenly, like a volcano, so it is liable to explode in anger.

clue.text: Chapel presents old exotic detective with test

parts.note: Charlie Chan was the Chinese-American detective of 1920s-40s novels and films
try means to test or attempt

explanation.surface: A chapel offers a vintage detective a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A chantry is a chapel endowed for priests to sing masses for the founder's soul.

clue.text: Virtuoso passage from A Study into Catholic South Africa

indicators.note: into means the first pieces are set inside the following ones

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: A showy passage drawn from a study of Catholic South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' places the article and the study between the Catholic and the country code. 'Study' looks like a piece of research, but it is a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a flourish for the soloist near the end of a concerto movement, showing off technique.

clue.text: Turnover, spectacular at first, is contained by Pacific island

indicators.note: is contained by means the chosen letter sits inside the island

parts.note: Samoa is an island nation in the South Pacific

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of spectacular

explanation.surface: A dramatic upheaval, spectacular at first, is held in check on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives S; 'is contained by' places it within SAMOA. 'Turnover' suggests a change; it is a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried pastry folded over a spicy filling, a kind of turnover.

clue.text: Sports event official's broadcast from another planet

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken aloud, so we want a word sounding like the official

parts.note: a marshal keeps order at races and other sporting events

explanation.surface: A sports steward's transmission comes from another world.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is'. Martial, from Mars, can mean of that planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial derives from Mars and can describe things belonging to the red planet.

clue.text: MacLean's editorial houses purged

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An editorial by MacLean shelters people who have been expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' signals letters held inside 'MacLean's editorial'. 'purged' looks like a past tense of expelling; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to clean thoroughly, so something purged has been made clean.

clue.text: Husband has love competition, a poet

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
a race is a contest

explanation.surface: A married man with a passion for competing, who also writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was the Roman lyric poet of the Odes and Satires.

clue.text: Division of school hard by river

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and another in East Anglia

explanation.surface: A school division located right beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: British schools group pupils into houses that compete with each other, so a house is one section.

clue.text: College tour around yard

indicators.note: around means the last letter of tour comes round to the front of the others

explanation.surface: A college tour goes round the grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' moves the last letter of the tour to its front. 'College' tempts as the definition, since Cambridge colleges have courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A court is an open area enclosed by walls or buildings, as a courtyard is.

clue.text: Old-time Royal Variety performer?

parts.note: suggests an act in the Royal Variety Performance, the annual British charity show before royalty, but means a medieval court entertainer

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Variety Performance is an annual British TV show in front of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A court fool amused medieval monarchs, a royal entertainer of the variety kind.

clue.text: Guardian follows one into unlit derelict submarine

indicators.note: follows means the newspaper's word comes after the rest
into means the single letter goes inside the jumbled letters
derelict means broken down, so the letters of unlit are in ruins and rearranged

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article
the Guardian, where this puzzle appears, refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A newspaper trails someone into a darkened, abandoned submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derelict' gives NUTIL, opened by 'into' for the single letter; 'follows' puts the paper's self-reference last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nautilus was Captain Nemo's craft in Jules Verne and later a US nuclear sub.

clue.text: Stiffener, for instance, taken over time

indicators.note: taken over means the next piece is absorbed inside the words for instance

parts.note: say means for example or for instance

explanation.surface: A stiffening agent, such as one absorbed over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' puts T inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a strip of bone or steel in a corset or collar that gives it rigidity.

clue.text: Instrument George Michael and mate finally installed in apartment

indicators.note: installed in means the pieces are fitted inside the apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: finally picks the last letters of the words Michael and mate

explanation.surface: Singer George Michael and his partner end up living in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the end letters of Michael and mate; 'installed in' fits them, after the abbreviation for George, into the apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small wind instrument like a recorder, with finger holes.
